sources.entry: Google Ads Transparency MCP - MCP server that gives AI assistants a competitor's Google ads from the Google Ads Transparency Center: new, running or stopped, with first and last shown dates; runs on your own Apify token. #opensource #mcp

summary.one_liner: An MCP server that lets AI assistants pull a competitor's Google ads from the Google Ads Transparency Center, showing which are new, running or stopped, via a hosted Apify Actor.
keywords: see what ads a competitor runs
find new ads from a rival
summary.what_it_does: The server takes a website domain, a Google advertiser ID, an Ads Transparency Center link, or an exact advertiser name and returns the ads Google lists for that advertiser. Each ad is labeled new, still running, or stopped within a configurable look-back window, with first and last shown dates, days shown, and a link to the ad. Results can be filtered by country or left set to anywhere. The tool returns one row per ad with advertiser, ad ID, format (text, image, or video), status, and target domain. The README says the data comes from the public Google Ads Transparency Center via the Apify Actor Google Ads Transparency Scraper, and no Google login or proxy setup is needed. The repo also includes a local stdio server (Node.js) and a Python version that forward tool calls to the hosted endpoint using the user's own Apify token.
use_cases: Check which Google ads a competitor started running recently
Compare live ads between two or more brands
Review ads a rival stopped running this month
Monitor competitor ad activity from an AI assistant
Pull ad links and shown dates for competitive research
how_to_run: Claude Code: claude mcp add --transport http google-ads-transparency "<MCP endpoint URL>"
Claude Desktop / claude.ai: Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector, paste the MCP endpoint URL
Cursor: add the endpoint URL under mcpServers in ~/.cursor/mcp.json
Local stdio: npx -y github:GeminiGeorge22/google-ads-transparency-mcp with env APIFY_TOKEN set
Python: uvx google-ads-transparency-mcp-server (or pip install google-ads-transparency-mcp-server), with APIFY_TOKEN set
notable: Accepts a domain, advertiser ID, Transparency Center link, or exact advertiser name as input
Classifies ads as new, running, or stopped within a look-back window with first and last shown dates
Runs on the user's own Apify token; OAuth or Bearer token auth on the hosted endpoint
Local stdio server answers tool listing from a bundled tools.json without any token
caveats: Requires an Apify account and API token; tool calls are not run without one
Data comes from the Google Ads Transparency Center via a third-party Actor, so coverage depends on what Google lists
The author states they maintain the Actor (disclosure in README)
